Use double quotes only when you intentionally want shell variables to be expanded:

cat > data.txt
# parameters
dt = 0.01
nsteps = 100
restart = false
file = results.dat
path = /home/m.sega/data
step 0 time 0.00 value 1.2
step 1 time 0.10 value 1.4
step 2 time 0.20 value 1.7
status OK
status WARNING
status FAILED
^D

grep -E '^step' data.txt
grep -E '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' data.txt
grep -E '^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*[[:space:]]*=' data.txt
grep -E 'status (OK|WARNING|FAILED)' data.txt
grep -Ev '^[[:space:]]*#' data.txt
sed -E 's/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/FLOAT/g' data.txt
sed -E 's/^restart[[:space:]]*=.*/restart = true/' data.txt
sed -E 's|/home/m\.sega/data|/scratch/m.sega/data|' data.txt
sed -E 's/^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*(.*)$/\1 -> \2/' data.txt
These commands cover the most common uses of regular expressions in shell text processing.
